original_question: Over a number field K, can one construct infinite families of generalized Hénon maps of algebraic degree d together with K-rational cycles of length at least d + 3, or even examples with N_d periodic points where N_d - d tends to infinity or N_d / d tends to infinity as d tends to infinity?
target_in_paper: Section 11, Question 46: the arithmetic open problem asking whether, over a number field K, one can construct generalized Hénon maps of algebraic degree d with K-rational cycles of length at least d+3, and more generally with many periodic points as d grows. The immediately preceding paragraph explains the motivating baseline construction, which yields cycles of length deg(F)+2 for maps f(x,y)=(y,F(y)-δx), while the definitions of "generalized Hénon map" and "algebraic degree" come from Section 6.1. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~buff/Preprints/Henon/Henon.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s exact target: it correctly identifies the base field as a number field K, the objects as generalized Hénon maps, the degree parameter d, the threshold d+3 for the cycle length, and the two asymptotic alternatives N_d-d→∞ and N_d/d→∞ as d→∞. In substance, it is a near-paraphrase of Question 46 in Section 11. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~buff/Preprints/Henon/Henon.pdf))
missing_details: The paper’s exact target is Section 11, Question 46; it is posed as an open question, not as a conjecture or theorem. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~buff/Preprints/Henon/Henon.pdf))

"Generalized Hénon map" is not defined in your draft. In the paper, a generalized Hénon map is a finite composition H_{a_1,P_1}∘⋯∘H_{a_k,P_k} of Hénon maps H_{a,P}(x,y)=(ay+P(x),x), and its algebraic degree is deg(f)=deg(P_1)⋯deg(P_k). ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~buff/Preprints/Henon/Henon.pdf))

The ambient space should be made explicit: these are polynomial automorphisms of the affine plane A^2 defined over K. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~buff/Preprints/Henon/Henon.pdf))

"K-rational cycle of length at least d+3" should be stated as a periodic cycle in A^2(K), ideally clarifying that the cycle length means exact period at least d+3. Question 46 itself leaves this implicit. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~buff/Preprints/Henon/Henon.pdf))

If one introduces N_d, one should say explicitly that N_d counts K-rational periodic points of f_d. In the nearby Conjecture 2, the paper explicitly writes Per(f) for periodic points over the algebraic closure, so a stand-alone restatement should remove that ambiguity. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~buff/Preprints/Henon/Henon.pdf))

The asymptotic clauses N_d-d→∞ and N_d/d→∞ require the family to be indexed by degrees d tending to infinity; your draft gestures at this, but a stand-alone version should say it explicitly. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~buff/Preprints/Henon/Henon.pdf))

The reason the bound d+3 is the relevant next threshold is hidden in the preceding context: the paper first explains a naive interpolation construction producing Hénon maps f(x,y)=(y,F(y)-δx) with cycles of length deg(F)+2. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~buff/Preprints/Henon/Henon.pdf))
refined_question: Fix a number field K. Does there exist an infinite family {f_d}_{d≥2} of generalized Hénon maps f_d:A^2_K→A^2_K, where each f_d is a finite composition of Hénon maps H_{a_i,P_i}(x,y)=(a_i y+P_i(x),x) with a_i∈K^* and P_i∈K[x], and where the algebraic degree satisfies deg(f_d)=∏_i deg(P_i)=d, such that f_d admits a K-rational periodic cycle of exact period at least d+3? More ambitiously, can one choose such maps so that the number N_d of K-rational periodic points of f_d satisfies N_d-d→∞, or even N_d/d→∞, as d→∞? ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~buff/Preprints/Henon/Henon.pdf))
justification: The draft is targeting Section 11, Question 46, and not one of the neighboring conjectures. The paper first observes that, over a sufficiently large field, a direct interpolation argument gives Hénon maps f(x,y)=(y,F(y)-δx) with cycles of length deg(F)+2; Question 46 then asks whether one can do better over a number field K, namely achieve K-rational cycles of length at least d+3, or even much larger numbers of periodic points as d grows. To make the question stand-alone while staying narrow and faithful, the only additions needed are the paper’s Section 6.1 definition of a generalized Hénon map and its algebraic degree, the ambient affine plane A^2_K, and an explicit statement that N_d counts K-rational periodic points. No alternate equivalent formulation is explicitly proved in the paper. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~buff/Preprints/Henon/Henon.pdf))
